title: The bottom navigation bar
why: It is app-owned chrome on every screen in the product, so a point of it is a point taken from every page. It is also the one surface where the reference's own decision is unambiguous: a hairline, a row of tabs, no pill.

masks.reason: Tab labels are translated. The label's box is compared; the glyphs inside it are not, because our Persian is not their English and never will be.

measurements.note: App-owned chrome only: the hairline plus the tab row. The system navigation inset is measured but never added in — see FoldMetricsTest for the same separation on our side.
A hairline is one physical pixel at this density or it is not a hairline.
Five equal columns. Weighted-by-content columns move every time the language changes, which is why ours are weight(1f) and why this is measured rather than assumed.

colour_samples.note: A fill, sampled at its centre. Never on an edge.

known_differences.label: INTENTIONAL_BRAND_DIFFERENCE
known_differences.what: The selected tab sits on a raised neutral plate rather than being marked by ink weight alone.
known_differences.why: The plate is what this design system's navigation rail already uses, so the two chromes agree with each other about what «you are here» looks like.

known_differences.label: INTENTIONAL_BRAND_DIFFERENCE
known_differences.what: Five destinations, with our own names and glyphs.
known_differences.why: Root navigation architecture is settled and out of scope for a parity pass.
